title: Reading Poetry Slowly
text:
Many readers find poetry difficult at first. A poem often uses short lines, unusual word order, and images that suggest more than they say. For example, a poet might compare a lonely street to a river without ever using the word 'like'.

The best way to read a poem is slowly and more than once. Reading aloud can help the reader hear the rhythm. After several readings, the meaning often becomes clearer, and the reader may notice details that were missed before.

questions.text: According to paragraph one, what do poems often use?
options: short lines and unusual word order

questions.text: According to paragraph two, how should a poem be read?
options: in one sitting with no notes

questions.text: Why might a poet compare a lonely street to a river?
options: to describe a real river nearby
to suggest a feeling without stating it directly
to explain how streets are built
to give a scientific fact about water

questions.text: What does the passage imply about reading a poem aloud?
options: It is useless for understanding poetry
It can help readers notice the rhythm
It should only be done by poets

vocabulary.definition: a regular pattern of sounds in speech or poetry
to indicate something without saying it directly

paragraph_translations:
Birçok okuyucu şiiri başta zor bulur. Bir şiir genellikle kısa dizeler, alışılmadık kelime sırası ve söylediklerinden daha fazlasını ima eden imgeler kullanır. Örneğin, bir şair ıssız bir sokağı, 'gibi' kelimesini hiç kullanmadan bir nehre benzetebilir.

Bir şiiri okumanın en iyi yolu yavaş ve birden fazla kez okumaktır. Sesli okumak, okuyucunun ritmi duymasına yardımcı olabilir. Birkaç okumadan sonra anlam genellikle daha net hale gelir ve okuyucu daha önce kaçırdığı ayrıntıları fark edebilir.
